TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Chel.]
Mucous pasty taste. θ Prosopalgia.
Taste : bitter ; insipid ; pappy ; acid.
Taste disgusting or bitter, but not of food or drink.
Taste in mouth bitter, food tasting natural.
Bitter taste in mouth. θ Hepatitis. θ Mental affections.
Metallic sour taste.
Speech difficult and unintelligible.
Tongue narrow, pointed. θ Dyspepsia.
Tongue dried up, brown, cracked. θ Influenza. θ Pneumonia.
Tongue inordinately dry or moist, of good natural color, but slightly coated white and sometimes streaky, the shape of it being narrow and pointed. θ Dyspepsia.
Tongue pale, moist, whitish. θ Intestinal catarrh.
Tongue red on edges and tip.
Tongue red and sore with raised papillæ. θ Typhus.
Tongue slimy, coated white or grey.
Tongue thickly coated yellow, with red margin, showing imprint of teeth.
Tongue covered with thick yellow fur. θ Laryngitis. θ Intestinal catarrh. θ Erysipelas.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Chel.]
Dryness of mouth. θ Liver complaint.
Burning in mouth.
Salivation, with nausea and giddiness.
Bitter water collects in mouth.
Mucus in mouth and tough mucous saliva.
Mucus flies from mouth when coughing.
Bad odor from mouth.
Oozing of blood from mucous membrane of mouth ; hemorrhagic vesicles, also hemorrhage from bowels and urethra. θ Bilious fever.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Chel.]
Sore tonsils. θ Hepatitis.
Fauces red ; uvula and tonsils swollen ; shooting in tonsils.
Shooting, burning and scraping in throat.
Nose, tongue and throat dry. θ Influenza.
Dryness in throat, with increased thirst.
Difficult swallowing.
Choking sensation in throat, < by breathing.
Choking, as from hasty swallowing.
Great sense of tightness around neck, above larynx, as if parts were constricted, hindering deglutition, but not respiration.
Sensation in throat as after swallowing too large a morsel of food ; as if a foreign body was rising in throat, which must be swallowed.
Hawking up lumps of phlegm, with sensation as if larynx was pressed upon, impeding swallowing.
Burning in œsophagus.
Secretion of thin mucus in œsophagus.
Venereal ulcers in throat.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Chel.]
Loss of appetite. θ Hepatic affections. θ Chorea. θ Influenza. θ Gastralgia. θ Erysipelas.
Loss of appetite, with vertigo and confusion of head. θ Chorea.
Loss of appetite, with disgust and nausea.
Great emaciation, with complete loss of appetite. θ Prosopalgia.
Thirst. θ Influenza. θ Erysipelas. θ Acute rheumatism. θ Pneumonia.
Thirst, with dry mouth ; or thirstlessness.
Thirst, with dryness of mouth and throat. θ Liver complaint.
Desire for sour things. θ Cardialgia.
Longing : for very hot drinks ; for wine or vinegar ; for milk ; for coffee ; for beer, which disagrees.
Dislike : to cheese ; to meat ; to coffee.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Chel.]
Milk improves ; wine relieves abdominal pain ; coffee agrees ; hot drinks agree ; cold drinks disagree.
Smoking causes burning and acidity from cardia to throat.
All complaints lessen after dinner.
Eating relieves pain in stomach and region of liver. θ Dyspepsia.
After dinner laziness and great dislike to work, with sleepiness.
